dedupe_keys.name: fcc mandatory disaster response initiative for wireless providers 2022 to 2024

description: This operations and policy case records how the US Federal Communications Commission turned a voluntary industry agreement on disaster cooperation into binding rules for mobile operators. From 2016 the Wireless Network Resiliency Cooperative Framework, a voluntary agreement among wireless carriers, promoted roaming, mutual aid and situational awareness in disasters; after its use in hurricanes and wildfires was reviewed, the Commission adopted the Mandatory Disaster Response Initiative in June 2022 (FCC 22-50), clarified it in September 2023 (FCC 23-71) and required compliance by 1 May 2024. The rules require facilities-based mobile providers to give each other roaming when a network is down where technically feasible, to sign mutual aid arrangements for sharing physical assets and consult before and during emergencies, to improve municipal preparedness and consumer readiness, and to report restoration times to the public and stakeholders, with the initiative triggered by Disaster Information Reporting System activations. Coverage: the United States, rules from 2022 with compliance in 2024. Format and access: free FCC orders, public notices and a Congressional Research Service brief. Caveats: the rules are recent, so evidence of effect is limited; roaming depends on technical feasibility. Simulation uses: operations and emergency response rules for restoring mobile service, recovery modelling with roaming and shared assets, and resilience of multi-operator networks. Related records: the FCC DIRS communications status reports give outage data during activations, and the Rogers outage review led to a similar roaming agreement in Canada.
